Maya-Sec: FYI spotted odd pattern in partner-ingest logs: multiple objects with KMS-wrapped payloads showing `cryptoKeyId=wrap-key-prod-01` and an unusual `additionalAuthenticatedData` field present. Posting here to coordinate triage.
Frank-Infra: can you paste a redacted sample line? want to see AAD shape.
Maya-Sec: redacted: `log: {resource: 'gs://partner-ingest/obj-2026-03-21', kms: {ciphertext: 'CiQ...REDACTED', cryptoKeyId: 'wrap-key-prod-01', aad: 'ingest-v2:batch-42'}}`
Jordan-SRE: That AAD looks like our ingestion pipeline stamp. Could be innocent, but multiple decrypt attempts from a single external IP in last 30m.
Lina-Eng: Is wrap-key-prod-01 the CMK used for Vault transit wrapping or a direct KMS-encrypted blob?
Frank-Infra: It's used both: Vault transit uses a wrapping key to envelope sealed secrets when we export backups; some ingestion jobs also call KMS directly with that key. Not ideal.
Maya-Sec: Risk: if an external party obtained ciphertext + can call KMS decrypt (via compromised creds), they can unwrap. Containment steps?
Jordan-SRE: Immediate containment: 1) add temporary IAM deny policy on that key for non-admin principals, 2) enable key-level CMEK audit logs if not already, 3) snapshot all objects referencing that key.
Frank-Infra: I'll push an IAM conditional deny binding: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding wrap-key-prod-01 --member='allUsers' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' --condition='expression=false, title="temp-deny"'` (pseudo) — actually will use `set-iam-policy` with explicit denies via org policy shim. Will coordinate with org-iam.
Lina-Eng: We should also scale vault audit logging (transit path) and export to secure bucket for forensic analysis: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault-transit-audit.log` then `gsutil cp` to incident bucket.
Sam-DevEx: Patch for ingestion: add AAD validation so downstream unwrap only accepts ciphertexts with expected AAD prefix `ingest-v2:`. That reduces risk of replay. I can open a quick PR.
Maya-Sec: Good. Also: rotate any service accounts that have `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` scoped to ingestion. Shorten token lifetimes where possible.
Jordan-SRE: I'll list current principals with decrypt on that key: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy wrap-key-prod-01 --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role=="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter")'` and then start a revoke sweep.
Frank-Infra: Found a CI service account with broad decrypt rights: `ci-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Revoking now and creating a narrow-scoped token for ongoing CI jobs.
audit-bot: incident logged INC-2026-5250001234. Collected logs to gs://redwood-sec-incidents/5250001234/ and started forensic VM snapshot.
Maya-Sec: Flag: partner-ingest bucket had cross-account ACL during partner onboarding. Confirming whether partner creds had decryption rights.
Lina-Eng: Partner account only had object read on bucket historically, but check if any IAM policy binding gave them KMS access. Searching.
Jordan-SRE: I'm seeing a grant to `serviceAccount:partner-ingest@external-partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` from 2025-11-02. That explains external IP unwrap attempts.
Maya-Sec: Immediate action: remove that binding, snapshot access logs for that service account, rotate keys, and treat any secret that was wrapped with that key as potentially exposed.
Frank-Infra: Removing binding now: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding wrap-key-prod-01 --member='serviceAccount:partner-ingest@external-partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter'`
Sam-DevEx: For rollout: we should separate the wrap keys used by Vault from keys used in the partner pipeline. Propose create `wrap-key-vault-prod` and `wrap-key-ingest-prod` and migrate.
Lina-Eng: Agreed. Migration plan: create new key(s), do a controlled rewrap for Vault exports and for any affected objects in partner bucket, validate checksums, and update configs. We'll also add a key policy that forbids cross-project grants.
Jordan-SRE: Rewrap tooling note: use KMS decrypt of old key with a privileged ephemeral VM that has just-in-time access, then encrypt with new key, avoid writing plaintext to disk. Use in-memory streams or ephemeral memory-only processes.
Maya-Sec: Also run threat intel enrichment on the external IP; add to blocklist for partner network and escalate to partner SOC.
Frank-Infra: Scheduling maintenance window 02:30 UTC to rotate keys and run migration scripts. Will post to #eng-oncall and notify partner.
Maya-Sec: Post-action items I'll own: 1) full inventory of secrets referencing wrap-key-prod-01, 2) RBAC hardening doc for KMS keys, 3) postmortem with timeline and partner communication.
Sam-DevEx: I'll land the AAD validation patch and a small lint that prevents using the production wrap key directly from non-vault services.
Lina-Eng: After rewrap, we'll add a BigQuery audit sink with alerts for Decrypt RPCs exceeding threshold and a SIEM rule. Example filter: `protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND resource.labels.crypto_key_id:"wrap-key-prod-01"`.
Jordan-SRE: Confirmed: snapshot complete, partner binding removed, and key-level deny applied to non-admins. Running smoke decrypts against new wrap-key-ingest-prod.
audit-bot: evidence bundle uploaded. Incident status: containment underway.
Maya-Sec: Thanks all — keep thread updated with any anomalies. Will schedule a post-incident review after containment. :lock:
